canonical_name: Mars Pathfinder priority inversion (1997) as Holzmann's Promela model, checked with SPIN 6.5.2
lineage: A REAL historical failure: the Mars Pathfinder lander (1997) suffered repeated system resets because a low-priority meteorological task held a mutex needed by the high-priority bus-management task while a medium-priority task starved it -- classic priority inversion under VxWorks, fixed by enabling priority inheritance. Holzmann's Promela model (Examples/pathfinder.pml in the SPIN distribution) reproduces the invalid end state (deadlock) and the fix. The failing model is preserved AS FAILING; SPIN is the instrument.
era: 1997 (event); model in SPIN distributions since the 2000s
version: Spin version-6.5.2 tarball, Examples/pathfinder.pml (same artifact as spin-6.5.2-holzmann)
entry_points: spin -a Examples/pathfinder.pml; gcc -o pan pan.c; ./pan  -> 'invalid end state' with the failing schedule; spin -t -p replays it

example.command: cd Src && make; cd ../Examples && ../Src/spin -a pathfinder.pml && gcc -o pan pan.c && ./pan
example.input: the model with priority inheritance off
example.output: pan: invalid end state (system deadlock); the trail shows the inversion

upstream_docs: Holzmann, The SPIN Model Checker, 2003 (the Pathfinder example)
Reeves, What really happened on Mars?, JPL 1997 (the incident account)
Sha, Rajkumar, Lehoczky, Priority Inheritance Protocols, IEEE TC 1990

human_capability_summary.built_to: share a resource between tasks of different priority on a real-time scheduler without the high-priority task being blocked indefinitely
human_capability_summary.pressure: hard deadlines (the watchdog resets the system), a shared bus with a mutex, three priority levels competing for the CPU
human_capability_summary.success_means: the high-priority task always gets the mutex within its deadline; the human record: without priority inheritance it did not, and the spacecraft reset

known_human_problem_solved: real-time mutual exclusion across priority levels
human_environmental_pressure: hard timing bounds, resource contention across priorities, a watchdog that treats delay as failure
human_failure_condition: priority inversion: the medium task runs, the low task holds the lock, the high task misses its deadline; the watchdog resets the lander
behavioral_entry_point: toggle the priority-inheritance option in pathfinder.pml (the model's own switch) and re-run pan: deadlock present vs absent

lineage_relations.note: the same tarball; this specimen is the failing model, that one is the checker

lineage_relations.to: Sha, Rajkumar, Lehoczky 1990 (the fix: priority inheritance)

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run spin-pathfinder-priority-inversion-1997
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: share a resource between tasks of different priority on a real-time scheduler without the high-priority task being blocked indefinitely
